title_en: Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted to strengthen drug administration, ensure drug quality, safeguard public medication safety and legitimate rights and interests, and protect and promote public health.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to activities such as drug research and development, production, distribution, use, and supervision and administration conducted within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
For the purposes of this Law, "drugs" refer to substances that are used for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of human diseases, intended to regulate human physiological functions, and have specified indications or functions, usage, and dosage, including traditional Chinese medicines, chemical drugs, and biological products.

Article 3 Drug administration shall center on people's health, adhere to the principles of risk management, whole-process control, and social co-governance, establish a scientific and strict supervision and administration system, comprehensively improve drug quality, and ensure the safety, efficacy, and accessibility of drugs.

Article 4 The State shall develop modern drugs and traditional drugs and give full play to their roles in prevention, treatment, and healthcare.
The State shall protect wild medicinal resources and traditional Chinese medicine varieties, and encourage the cultivation of authentic medicinal herbs.

Article 5 The State shall encourage research and innovation of new drugs, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations in researching and developing new drugs.

Article 6 The State shall implement a drug marketing authorization holder system for drug administration. The drug marketing authorization holder shall, in accordance with law, be responsible for the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of drugs throughout the entire process of research and development, production, distribution, and use.

Article 7 Entities engaged in drug research and development, production, distribution, and use activities shall comply with laws, regulations, rules, standards, and norms, and ensure that information throughout the entire process is true, accurate, complete, and traceable.

Article 8 The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall be in charge of nationwide drug supervision and administration. Relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for drug-related supervision and administration within their respective functions. The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall coordinate with relevant departments of the State Council to implement national drug industry development plans and industrial policies.
The drug regulatory authorities of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be responsible for drug supervision and administration within their respective administrative regions. The departments responsible for drug supervision and administration of the people's governments of cities divided into districts and counties (hereinafter referred to as drug regulatory authorities) shall be responsible for drug supervision and administration within their respective administrative regions. Relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for drug-related supervision and administration within their respective functions.

Article 9 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for drug supervision and administration within their respective administrative regions, uniformly lead, organize, and coordinate drug supervision and administration work and response to drug safety emergencies within their respective administrative regions, and establish and improve the drug supervision and administration mechanism and information sharing mechanism.

Article 10 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate drug safety work into the national economic and social development plan at the same level, include drug safety work funds in the government budget at the same level, strengthen the capacity building for drug supervision and administration, and provide guarantee for drug safety work.

Article 11 Professional drug technical institutions established or designated by the drug regulatory authority shall undertake work such as review, inspection, verification, monitoring, and evaluation required for the implementation of drug supervision and administration in accordance with law.

Article 12 The State shall establish and improve a drug traceability system. The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall formulate unified drug traceability standards and norms, promote the exchange and sharing of drug traceability information, and achieve traceability of drugs.
The State shall establish a pharmacovigilance system to monitor, identify, assess, and control adverse drug reactions and other harmful reactions related to drug use.

Article 13 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, drug industry associations, etc. shall strengthen drug safety publicity and education, and carry out popularization of drug safety laws, regulations, and other knowledge.
News media shall conduct public service publicity on drug safety laws, regulations, and other knowledge, and exercise public oversight over illegal drug activities. Reports and publicity concerning drugs shall be comprehensive, scientific, objective, and fair.

Article 14 Drug industry associations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, establish and improve industry norms, promote the construction of an industry integrity system, and guide and urge members to carry out drug production, distribution, and other activities in accordance with law.

Article 15 People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall, in accordance with relevant state provisions, commend and reward units and individuals that have made outstanding contributions in drug research and development, production, distribution, use, and supervision and administration.

Article 16 The State shall support drug innovation guided by clinical value and having clear or special efficacy on human diseases, encourage the research and development of new drugs with new therapeutic mechanisms, treating life-threatening diseases or rare diseases, and having multi-target systemic regulatory intervention functions on the human body, and promote the advancement of drug technology.
The State shall encourage the use of modern science and technology and traditional Chinese medicine research methods to carry out scientific and technological research and drug development of traditional Chinese medicine, establish and improve a technical evaluation system that conforms to the characteristics of traditional Chinese medicine, and promote the inheritance and innovation of traditional Chinese medicine.
The State shall take effective measures to encourage the research and development and innovation of drugs for children, support the development of new varieties, dosage forms, and specifications of drugs for children that conform to children's physiological characteristics, and give priority to the review and approval of drugs for children.

Article 17 Entities engaged in drug research and development activities shall comply with the good laboratory practice for non-clinical studies and the good clinical practice for drug clinical trials, and ensure that the entire process of drug research and development continuously meets the statutory requirements.
The good laboratory practice for non-clinical studies and the good clinical practice for drug clinical trials shall be formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 18 Conducting non-clinical studies shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State, have personnel, sites, equipment, instruments, and management systems suitable for the research project, and ensure the authenticity of relevant data, materials, and samples.

Article 19 To conduct drug clinical trials, the applicant shall truthfully submit relevant data, materials, and samples such as research methods, quality indicators, pharmacological and toxicological test results to the drug regulatory authority of the State Council in accordance with its provisions, and obtain approval from the drug regulatory authority of the State Council. The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall decide whether to consent and notify the clinical trial sponsor within sixty working days from the date of receipt of the clinical trial application. If no notification is given within the time limit, it shall be deemed as consent. For the conduct of bioequivalence tests, the applicant shall file them with the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.
Drug clinical trials shall be conducted in clinical trial institutions that meet the corresponding conditions. Clinical trial institutions for drugs shall be managed by a filing system. The specific measures shall be jointly formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and the health department of the State Council.

Article 20 Conducting drug clinical trials shall comply with ethical principles, develop clinical trial protocols, and obtain review and approval from the ethics committee.
The ethics committee shall establish an ethical review work system, ensure that the ethical review process is independent, objective, and fair, supervise the standardized conduct of drug clinical trials, protect the legitimate rights and interests of subjects, and safeguard the public interest.

Article 21 When conducting drug clinical trials, the party shall truthfully explain and clarify to the subjects or their guardians the details such as the purpose and risks of the clinical trial, obtain the informed consent form voluntarily signed by the subjects or their guardians, and take effective measures to protect the lawful rights and interests of the subjects.

Article 22 During the period of drug clinical trials, if safety issues or other risks are discovered, the clinical trial sponsor shall timely adjust the clinical trial protocol, suspend or terminate the clinical trial, and report to the drug regulatory authority of the State Council. When necessary, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council may order the adjustment of the clinical trial protocol, suspension or termination of the clinical trial.

Article 23 For drugs being used in ongoing clinical trials for the treatment of diseases that seriously endanger life and for which there is no effective treatment, if medical observation indicates potential benefit and it complies with ethical principles, after review and informed consent, it may be used for other patients with the same condition within the institution conducting the clinical trial.

Article 24 For drugs marketed within the territory of China, approval shall be obtained from the drug regulatory authority of the State Council and a drug registration certificate shall be obtained; however, Chinese medicinal materials and Chinese medicine decoction pieces that are not subject to approval administration are excluded. The catalogue of varieties of Chinese medicinal materials and Chinese medicine decoction pieces subject to approval administration shall be formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the competent department of traditional Chinese medicine of the State Council.
When applying for drug registration, true, sufficient, and reliable data, information, and samples shall be provided to demonstrate the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of the drug.

Article 25 For drugs applying for registration, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall organize pharmaceutical, medical, and other technical personnel to conduct evaluation, and shall examine the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of the drug as well as the applicant's capabilities in quality management, risk prevention and control, and liability compensation; where conditions are met, a drug registration certificate shall be issued.
When the drug regulatory authority of the State Council examines and approves drugs, it shall simultaneously evaluate and approve chemical active pharmaceutical ingredients, evaluate relevant excipients, packaging materials and containers that directly contact the drug, and concurrently approve drug quality standards, production processes, labels, and package inserts.
For the purposes of this Law, excipients refer to the vehicles and additives used in the production of drugs and the preparation of prescriptions.

Article 26 For drugs for the treatment of diseases that seriously endanger life and for which there is no effective treatment, and for drugs urgently needed in public health, if data from drug clinical trials have shown efficacy and can predict their clinical value, conditional approval may be granted, and relevant matters shall be stated in the drug registration certificate.

Article 27 The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall improve the drug evaluation and approval work system, strengthen capacity building, establish and improve mechanisms such as communication and expert consultation, optimize the evaluation and approval process, and enhance the efficiency of evaluation and approval.
The evaluation conclusions and bases for drugs approved for marketing shall be made public according to law and subject to public supervision. Trade secrets learned during evaluation and approval shall be kept confidential.

Article 28 Drugs shall comply with the national drug standards. Where the drug quality standards approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council are higher than the national drug standards, the approved drug quality standards shall be followed; where there are no national drug standards, the approved drug quality standards shall be complied with.
The Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China and the drug standards promulgated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council are the national drug standards.
The drug regulatory authority of the State Council, jointly with the competent health department of the State Council, shall organize a pharmacopoeia committee responsible for the formulation and revision of national drug standards.
The drug testing institution established or designated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall be responsible for the calibration of national drug standard substances and reference standards.

Article 29 The name of a drug included in the national drug standards is the generic name of the drug. Where a name has been used as a generic name of a drug, such name shall not be used as a drug trademark.

Article 30 A drug marketing authorization holder refers to an enterprise or a drug research and development institution that has obtained a drug registration certificate.
The drug marketing authorization holder shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, assume responsibility for non-clinical research, clinical trials, production and operation, post-marketing research, adverse reaction monitoring and reporting and handling of the drug. Other entities and individuals engaged in drug research and development, production, operation, storage, transportation, use and other activities shall bear corresponding responsibility according to law.
The legal representative and principal person in charge of the drug marketing authorization holder shall be fully responsible for drug quality.

Article 31 The drug marketing authorization holder shall establish a drug quality assurance system and assign dedicated personnel to independently be responsible for drug quality management.
The drug marketing authorization holder shall conduct regular audits of the quality management systems of entrusted drug manufacturers and drug distributors, and supervise their continuous possession of quality assurance and control capabilities.

Article 32 A drug marketing authorization holder may produce drugs by itself or may entrust a drug manufacturer to produce drugs.
Where the drug marketing authorization holder produces drugs by itself, it shall obtain a drug production license in accordance with the provisions of this Law; where it entrusts production, it shall entrust a qualified drug manufacturer. The drug marketing authorization holder and the entrusted manufacturer shall sign an entrustment agreement and a quality agreement, and strictly perform the obligations stipulated in the agreements.
The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall formulate guidelines for drug entrusted production quality agreements to guide and supervise the drug marketing authorization holder and the entrusted manufacturer in fulfilling drug quality assurance obligations.
Blood products, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, toxic drugs for medical use, and precursor chemicals for drugs shall not be entrusted for production; unless otherwise provided by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 33 The drug marketing authorization holder shall establish drug marketing release procedures, audit the drugs released from the factory by the drug manufacturer, and release them only after being signed by the qualified person. Drugs that do not comply with national drug standards shall not be released.

Article 34 A drug marketing authorization holder may sell by itself the drugs for which it has obtained drug registration certificates, or may entrust a drug distributor to sell them. If a drug marketing authorization holder engages in drug retail activities, it shall obtain a drug distribution license.
Where the drug marketing authorization holder sells drugs by itself, it shall meet the conditions stipulated in Article 52 of this Law; where it entrusts sales, it shall entrust a qualified drug distributor. The drug marketing authorization holder and the entrusted distributor shall sign an entrustment agreement and strictly perform the obligations stipulated in the agreement.

Article 35 Where a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, or drug distributor entrusts the storage or transportation of drugs, it shall evaluate the quality assurance capability and risk management capability of the trustee, sign an entrustment agreement with it, stipulate the drug quality responsibilities, operating procedures, and other contents, and supervise the trustee.

Article 36 Drug marketing authorization holders, drug manufacturers, drug distributors, and medical institutions shall establish and implement a drug traceability system, provide traceability information in accordance with regulations, and ensure that drugs are traceable.

Article 37 The drug marketing authorization holder shall establish an annual reporting system, and report annually on drug production and sales, post-marketing research, risk management, and other circumstances to the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in accordance with regulations.

Article 38 Where the drug marketing authorization holder is an overseas enterprise, the enterprise legal person designated by it within China shall perform the obligations of the drug marketing authorization holder and bear joint and several liability with the drug marketing authorization holder.

Article 39 Chinese medicine decoction piece manufacturers shall perform the relevant obligations of drug marketing authorization holders, implement whole-process management over the production and sale of Chinese medicine decoction pieces, establish a traceability system for Chinese medicine decoction pieces, and ensure that Chinese medicine decoction pieces are safe, effective, and traceable.

Article 40 With the approval of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council, a drug marketing authorization holder may transfer the drug marketing authorization. The transferee shall have the capabilities of quality management, risk prevention and control, and liability compensation to ensure the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of the drug, and shall perform the obligations of the drug marketing authorization holder.

Article 41. Engaging in drug production activities shall be subject to the approval of the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the entity is located, and a drug production license shall be obtained. Without a drug production license, no drug production shall be conducted.
The drug production license shall indicate the validity period and production scope, and shall be reviewed and reissued upon expiration.

Article 43. Engaging in drug production activities shall comply with the Good Manufacturing Practice for drugs, establish and improve the drug production quality management system, and ensure that the entire process of drug production continuously meets the statutory requirements.
The legal representative and the principal responsible person of a drug manufacturer shall assume full responsibility for the drug production activities of the enterprise.

Article 44. Drugs shall be produced in accordance with the national drug standards and the production processes approved by the drug regulatory department. Production and inspection records shall be complete and accurate, and shall not be fabricated.
Decoction pieces of Chinese crude drugs shall be processed in accordance with the national drug standards; where the national drug standards have no provisions, they shall be processed in accordance with the processing specifications formulated by the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government. The processing specifications formulated by the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be filed with the drug regulatory department of the State Council. Those that do not conform to the national drug standards or are not processed in accordance with the processing specifications formulated by the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall not be released from factories or sold.

Article 45. The raw materials and auxiliary materials required for drug production shall meet the requirements for medicinal use and the relevant requirements of the Good Manufacturing Practice for drugs.
When producing drugs, the suppliers of raw materials, auxiliary materials, etc. shall be audited in accordance with the provisions to ensure that the purchased and used raw materials, auxiliary materials, etc. meet the requirements specified in the preceding paragraph.

Article 46. Packaging materials and containers that come into direct contact with drugs shall meet the requirements for medicinal use and the standards for protecting human health and safety.
The drug regulatory department shall order the cessation of use of non-compliant packaging materials and containers that come into direct contact with drugs.

Article 47. A drug manufacturer shall conduct quality inspection of drugs. Those that do not conform to the national drug standards shall not be released from factories.
A drug manufacturer shall establish a drug release procedure, specifying the standards and conditions for release. Only after being signed by the qualified person may the drugs be released if they meet the standards and conditions.

Article 48. Drug packaging shall be suitable for the quality requirements of the drugs and facilitate storage, transportation and medical use.
Chinese crude drugs to be dispatched shall be packaged. On each package, the name, place of origin, date, supplying unit shall be indicated, and a quality conformity mark shall be attached.

Article 49. Drug packaging shall be printed or affixed with a label and accompanied by a package insert in accordance with the provisions.
The label or package insert shall indicate the generic name, ingredients, specifications, marketing authorization holder and its address, manufacturer and its address, approval number, batch number, production date, expiry date, indications or functions and indications, usage, dosage, contraindications, adverse reactions and precautions. The text on the label and package insert shall be legible, and items such as production date and expiry date shall be prominently marked and easily identifiable.
Labels and package inserts of narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, toxic drugs for medical use, radioactive drugs, drugs for external use and non-prescription drugs shall be printed with the prescribed symbols.

Article 50. Personnel who have direct contact with drugs in the marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor and medical institution shall undergo annual health examinations. Those suffering from infectious diseases or other diseases that may contaminate drugs shall not engage in work that involves direct contact with drugs.

Article 51. Engaging in drug wholesale activities shall be subject to the approval of the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the entity is located, and a drug distribution license shall be obtained. Engaging in drug retail activities shall be subject to the approval of the drug regulatory department of the local people's government at or above the county level where the entity is located, and a drug distribution license shall be obtained. Without a drug distribution license, no drug distribution shall be conducted.
The drug distribution license shall indicate the validity period and scope of distribution, and shall be reviewed and reissued upon expiration.
When implementing drug distribution licensing, the drug regulatory department shall, in addition to following the conditions specified in Article 52 of this Law, also adhere to the principle of facilitating the purchase of drugs by the public.

Article 53. Engaging in drug distribution activities shall comply with the Good Supply Practice for drugs, establish and improve the drug distribution quality management system, and ensure that the entire process of drug distribution continuously meets the statutory requirements.
The State encourages and guides chain operation in drug retail. The headquarters of enterprises engaged in chain operation of drug retail shall establish a unified quality management system and fulfill management responsibilities over the distribution activities of their subordinate retail enterprises.
The legal representative and the principal responsible person of a drug distributor shall assume full responsibility for the drug distribution activities of the enterprise.

Article 54. The State implements a classification management system for prescription drugs and non-prescription drugs. The specific measures shall be formulated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the health authority of the State Council.

Article 55. Marketing authorization holders, drug manufacturers, drug distributors and medical institutions shall purchase drugs from marketing authorization holders or enterprises with drug production or distribution qualifications; however, this does not apply to the purchase of Chinese crude drugs not subject to approval administration.

Article 56. A drug distributor that purchases drugs shall establish and implement a purchase inspection and acceptance system to verify drug conformity certificates and other markings; those that do not meet the prescribed requirements shall not be purchased or sold.

Article 57. A drug distributor that purchases and sells drugs shall maintain true and complete purchase and sale records. The purchase and sale records shall indicate the generic name, dosage form, specifications, batch number, expiry date, marketing authorization holder, manufacturer, purchasing and selling entities, quantity, price, date of purchase and sale, and other contents as prescribed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 58. A drug distributor that retails drugs shall do so accurately and correctly explain the usage, dosage and precautions. Dispensing of prescriptions shall be subject to verification, and the drugs listed in the prescription shall not be arbitrarily changed or substituted. A prescription with incompatibility or excessive dosage shall be refused for dispensing; if necessary, it may be dispensed only after it is corrected and re-signed by the prescribing physician.
A drug distributor that sells Chinese crude drugs shall indicate the place of origin.
Pharmacists or other pharmaceutical technical personnel who have been qualified according to law shall be responsible for the drug management, prescription review and dispensing, rational drug use guidance and other work of the enterprise.

Article 59. A drug distributor shall formulate and implement a drug storage system, take necessary measures such as refrigeration, anti-freezing, moisture-proof, insect-proof and rodent-proof measures to ensure drug quality.
Incoming and outgoing warehouse inspections shall be carried out in accordance with the inspection system.
Article 60. Chinese crude drugs may be sold in urban and rural trade markets, unless otherwise provided by the State Council.

Article 61 A drug marketing authorization holder or a drug distributor that sells drugs through the network shall comply with the relevant provisions of this Law on drug distribution. The specific administrative measures shall be formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the health authority of the State Council and other departments.
Vaccines, blood products, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, medicinal toxic drugs, radioactive drugs, precursor chemicals for pharmaceuticals, and other drugs subject to special administration by the State may not be sold online.

Article 62 The provider of a third-party platform for online drug transactions shall, in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council, file a record with the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where it is located.
The third-party platform provider shall, according to law, verify the qualifications of drug marketing authorization holders and drug distributors applying to operate on the platform, ensure that they meet the statutory requirements, and manage the drug distribution activities occurring on the platform.
Where a third-party platform provider discovers that a drug marketing authorization holder or a drug distributor operating on the platform has violated the provisions of this Law, it shall promptly stop such conduct and immediately report to the drug regulatory authority of the people's government at the county level where it is located; if a serious illegal act is discovered, it shall immediately cease providing the online trading platform services.
Article 63 Newly discovered medicinal materials and those introduced from abroad may be sold only after being approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 64 Drugs shall be imported through ports that permit the import of drugs, and the enterprise importing the drugs shall file a record with the drug regulatory authority at the location of the port. The customs shall handle the customs clearance procedures based on the import drug clearance certificate issued by the drug regulatory authority. In the absence of an import drug clearance certificate, the customs may not release the goods.
The drug regulatory authority at the location of the port shall notify the drug testing institution to conduct random inspection and testing of imported drugs in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.
The ports that permit the import of drugs shall be proposed by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the General Administration of Customs, and submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 65 Where a medical institution imports a small quantity of drugs due to urgent clinical needs, it may import them upon approval by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council or the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government authorized by the State Council. The imported drugs shall be used in designated medical institutions for specific medical purposes.
The carrying of a small quantity of drugs into the country for personal use shall be handled in accordance with the relevant regulations of the State.

Article 66 The import or export of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances within the scope prescribed by the State shall be subject to the possession of an import permit or export permit issued by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.
Article 67 The import of drugs with uncertain efficacy, serious adverse reactions, or that otherwise endanger human health is prohibited.

Article 68 The drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall designate a drug testing institution to inspect the following drugs before their sale or at the time of import; those that have not been inspected or have failed inspection may not be sold or imported:
(1) drugs marketed for the first time within the territory of China;
(2) biological products specified by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council; and
(3) other drugs specified by the State Council.

Article 69 A medical institution shall be staffed with pharmacists who have been legally qualified, or other pharmaceutical technical personnel, who shall be responsible for the drug management, prescription review and dispensing, and guidance on rational drug use of the institution. Non-pharmaceutical technical personnel may not directly engage in pharmaceutical technical work.

Article 70 When purchasing drugs, a medical institution shall establish and implement a system of inspection and acceptance upon receipt, verifying the certificates of conformity and other markings of the drugs; drugs that do not meet the prescribed requirements may not be purchased or used.

Article 71 A medical institution shall have premises, equipment, storage facilities, and sanitary conditions commensurate with the drugs used, formulate and implement a drug storage system, and take necessary measures such as cold storage, freeze protection, moisture protection, pest control, and rodent control to ensure drug quality.

Article 72 A medical institution shall adhere to the principles of safe, effective, economical, and rational drug use, follow the guiding principles for clinical drug application, clinical diagnosis and treatment guidelines, and drug instructions for rational use, and review the appropriateness of physicians' prescriptions and medication orders.
Other drug use entities other than medical institutions shall comply with the provisions of this Law concerning the use of drugs by medical institutions.

Article 73 A pharmacist or other pharmaceutical technical personnel who has been legally qualified and who dispenses a prescription shall check it, and may not arbitrarily alter or substitute the drugs listed in the prescription. For a prescription containing incompatibilities or exceeding the dosage, the pharmacist shall refuse to dispense it; where necessary, the prescription may be dispensed only after being corrected or re-signed by the prescribing physician.

Article 74 To prepare pharmaceutical preparations, a medical institution shall obtain approval from the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where it is located, and obtain a Medical Institution Pharmaceutical Preparation License. Without such a license, no pharmaceutical preparations may be prepared.
The Medical Institution Pharmaceutical Preparation License shall indicate its validity period and shall be re-examined and reissued upon expiration.

Article 75 To prepare pharmaceutical preparations, a medical institution shall have facilities, management systems, testing instruments, and sanitary conditions that can ensure the quality of the preparations.
Medical institutions shall prepare pharmaceutical preparations in accordance with the approved process, and the required raw materials, excipients, packaging materials, etc., shall meet pharmaceutical requirements.

Article 76 The pharmaceutical preparations prepared by a medical institution shall be those clinically needed by the institution but not available on the market, and shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where it is located; except where the law otherwise provides for the preparation of traditional Chinese medicine preparations.
Pharmaceutical preparations prepared by a medical institution shall undergo quality inspection in accordance with the provisions; those that pass the inspection may be used within the institution by virtue of a physician's prescription. With the approval of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council or the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the pharmaceutical preparations prepared by a medical institution may be transferred and used among designated medical institutions.
Pharmaceutical preparations prepared by a medical institution may not be sold on the market.

Article 77 A drug marketing authorization holder shall formulate a post-marketing risk management plan, proactively conduct post-marketing studies, further confirm the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of drugs, and strengthen the continuous management of marketed drugs.

Article 78 For drugs approved under conditions, the drug marketing authorization holder shall take corresponding risk management measures and complete relevant research in accordance with the requirements within the specified period; if the research is not completed within the period as required or if the holder cannot demonstrate that the benefits outweigh the risks, the drug regulatory authority of the State Council shall handle the matter according to law, up to and including revoking the drug registration certificate.

Article 79 Changes in the drug manufacturing process shall be subject to classified management based on the degree of risk and impact on drug safety, efficacy, and quality controllability. Major changes shall be approved by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council; other changes shall be filed or reported in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council.
A drug marketing authorization holder shall, in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory authority of the State Council, comprehensively assess and verify the impact of the changes on drug safety, efficacy, and quality controllability.

Article 80 A drug marketing authorization holder shall conduct post-marketing adverse drug reaction monitoring, proactively collect, track, and analyze information on suspected adverse drug reactions, and promptly take risk control measures for drugs with identified risks.

Article 81 A drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, and medical institution shall regularly examine the quality, efficacy, and adverse reactions of the drugs they produce, distribute, or use. Where any suspected adverse reaction is discovered, they shall promptly report it to the drug regulatory authority and the health administrative department. The specific measures shall be formulated by the drug regulatory authority under the State Council jointly with the health administrative department under the State Council.
For any drug that has been confirmed to cause serious adverse reactions, the drug regulatory authority under the State Council or the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall take emergency control measures such as suspending its production, distribution, or use based on the actual circumstances, and shall organize an expert evaluation within five days, and make an administrative decision according to law within fifteen days from the date of the evaluation conclusion.

Article 82 Where a drug has quality issues or other safety hazards, the drug marketing authorization holder shall immediately cease distribution, notify the relevant drug distributors and medical institutions to cease distribution and use, recall the drugs already distributed, disclose the recall information in a timely manner, and where necessary, immediately cease production, and report the drug recall and handling to the drug regulatory authority and the health administrative department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. Drug manufacturers, drug distributors, and medical institutions shall cooperate.
Where a drug marketing authorization holder fails to recall a drug that shall be recalled according to law, the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall order it to recall the drug.

Article 83 A drug marketing authorization holder shall regularly conduct post-marketing evaluation on the safety, efficacy, and quality controllability of marketed drugs. Where necessary, the drug regulatory authority under the State Council may order the drug marketing authorization holder to conduct post-marketing evaluation or directly organize and conduct post-marketing evaluation.
For any drug that, after evaluation, has uncertain efficacy, serious adverse reactions, or endangers human health for other reasons, its drug registration certificate shall be revoked.
A drug whose drug registration certificate has been revoked shall not be produced, imported, distributed, or used.
A drug whose drug registration certificate has been revoked, or which has exceeded its validity period, shall be destroyed under the supervision of the drug regulatory authority, or shall undergo other harmless treatment measures according to law.

Article 84 The State shall improve the drug procurement management system, monitor drug prices, conduct cost and price investigations, strengthen drug price supervision and inspection, investigate and punish drug price-related illegal acts such as price monopoly and price gouging according to law, and maintain the drug price order.

Article 85 For drugs whose prices are subject to market regulation according to law, the drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, and medical institution shall set prices in accordance with the principles of fairness, reasonableness, good faith, and correspondence between quality and price, and provide drugs at reasonable prices for drug users.
The drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, and medical institution shall comply with the regulations of the drug pricing authority under the State Council on drug price management, set and indicate the retail prices of drugs, and prohibit practices such as excessive profits, price monopoly, and price fraud.

Article 86 A drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, and medical institution shall, according to law, provide the drug pricing authority with information on actual purchase and sale prices and quantities of their drugs.

Article 87 A medical institution shall provide patients with a price list of drugs used, truthfully publish the prices of its commonly used drugs in accordance with regulations, and strengthen the management of rational drug use. The specific measures shall be formulated by the health administrative department under the State Council.

Article 88 It is prohibited for a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or medical institution to give or accept rebates or other improper benefits in drug purchasing and selling.
It is prohibited for a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or their agents to give, in any name, property or other improper benefits to persons in charge of medical institutions using their drugs, drug procurement personnel, physicians, pharmacists, or other relevant persons. It is prohibited for persons in charge of a medical institution, drug procurement personnel, physicians, pharmacists, or other relevant persons to accept, in any name, property or other improper benefits given by a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or their agents.

Article 89 A drug advertisement shall be approved by the advertisement examination authority designated by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the advertiser is located; without such approval, it shall not be published.

Article 90 The content of a drug advertisement shall be truthful and lawful, based on the drug package insert approved by the drug regulatory authority under the State Council, and shall not contain any false content.
A drug advertisement shall not contain any assertion or guarantee of efficacy or safety; shall not use the names or images of state organs, scientific research units, academic institutions, trade associations, or experts, scholars, physicians, pharmacists, patients, etc., for recommendation or certification.
Non-drug advertisements shall not contain any promotion involving drugs.

Article 91 For drug prices and advertisements, matters not provided for in this Law shall be governed by the provisions of the Price Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws.

Article 92 The State shall implement a drug reserve system and establish drug reserves at the central and local levels.
In the event of a major disaster, epidemic, or other emergency, drugs may be urgently requisitioned in accordance with the provisions of the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 93 The State shall implement an essential drug system, select an appropriate number of essential drug varieties, strengthen the organization of their production and reserve, enhance the supply capacity of essential drugs, and meet the basic drug needs for disease prevention and treatment.

Article 94 The State shall establish a drug supply and demand monitoring system, timely collect, aggregate, and analyze information on the supply and demand of drugs in shortage, issue early warnings for drugs in shortage, and take response measures.

Article 95 The State shall implement a list management system for drugs in shortage. The specific measures shall be formulated by the health administrative department under the State Council jointly with the drug regulatory authority under the State Council and other relevant departments.
Where a drug marketing authorization holder ceases production of a drug in shortage, it shall report to the drug regulatory authority under the State Council or the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in accordance with regulations.

Article 96 The State shall encourage the research, development, and production of drugs in shortage, and grant priority review and approval to drugs in shortage that are clinically urgently needed and new drugs for the prevention and treatment of major infectious diseases and rare diseases.

Article 97 For drugs in shortage, the State Council may restrict or prohibit their export. Where necessary, the relevant departments under the State Council may take measures such as organizing production, price intervention, and expanding import to ensure drug supply.
A drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, and drug distributor shall ensure the production and supply of drugs in accordance with regulations.

Article 99 The drug regulatory authority shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations, conduct supervision and inspection on activities such as drug research and development, production, distribution, and the use of drugs by drug-using entities, and where necessary, may extend the inspection to entities or individuals that provide products or services for drug research and development, production, distribution, or use. The relevant entities and individuals shall cooperate and shall not refuse or conceal information.
The drug regulatory authority shall implement key supervision and inspection on high-risk drugs.
Where there is evidence proving that potential safety hazards may exist, the drug regulatory authority shall, based on the supervision and inspection, take measures such as warnings, interviews, orders for rectification within a time limit, and suspension of production, distribution, use, or import, and shall promptly make public the results of the inspection and handling.
When conducting supervision and inspection, the drug regulatory authority shall present certification documents and shall keep confidential any trade secrets learned during the supervision and inspection.

Article 100 The drug regulatory authority may, as necessary for supervision and administration, conduct random inspection and testing on drug quality. Random inspection and testing shall sample in accordance with regulations and shall not charge any fees; the samples shall be purchased. The necessary expenses shall be allocated in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
For drugs and related materials that are proven to be potentially harmful to human health, the drug regulatory authority may seal up or seize them, and shall make an administrative decision within seven days; where the drug needs to be tested, the administrative decision shall be made within fifteen days from the issuance of the test report.

The drug regulatory department of the State Council and of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall regularly announce the results of drug quality spot checks and tests; if the announcement is improper, it shall make corrections within the original scope of the announcement.

If a party disagrees with the drug test result, it may, within seven days from the date of receiving the drug test result, apply for a re-test to the original drug testing institution or to a drug testing institution established or designated by the drug regulatory department at the next higher level, or may directly apply for a re-test to a drug testing institution established or designated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council. The drug testing institution that accepts the re-test shall issue a re-test conclusion within the time limit prescribed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

The drug regulatory department shall inspect the compliance of drug marketing authorization holders, drug manufacturers, drug distributors, and institutions for non-clinical safety evaluation of drugs, institutions for drug clinical trials, etc., with the Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs, Good Supply Practice for Drugs, Good Laboratory Practice for Non-clinical Studies, Good Clinical Practice for Drugs, and other requirements, and shall supervise them to continuously meet statutory requirements.
The State shall establish a professional and specialized team of drug inspectors. Inspectors shall be familiar with drug laws and regulations and possess professional drug knowledge.

The drug regulatory department shall establish drug safety credit files for drug marketing authorization holders, drug manufacturers, drug distributors, institutions for non-clinical safety evaluation of drugs, institutions for drug clinical trials, and medical institutions, recording information on the issuance of licenses, results of routine supervision and inspection, investigation and punishment of illegal acts, etc., and shall make such information public according to law and update it in a timely manner; for those with adverse credit records, the frequency of supervision and inspection shall be increased, and joint punishments may be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the State.

The drug regulatory department shall publish its email address and telephone number, accept consultations, complaints, and reports, and shall respond, verify, and handle them in a timely manner according to law. For reports verified to be true, the informant shall be rewarded in accordance with relevant provisions.
The drug regulatory department shall keep the informant's information confidential and protect the informant's legitimate rights and interests. If the informant reports his/her own unit, the unit shall not retaliate against the informant by means such as terminating or changing the labor contract or by other means.

The State implements a system of unified publication of drug safety information. The overall national drug safety situation, drug safety risk warning information, major drug safety incidents and their investigation and handling information, and other information determined by the State Council to be published uniformly shall be published uniformly by the drug regulatory department of the State Council. If the impact of drug safety risk warning information and major drug safety incidents and their investigation and handling information is limited to specific regions, such information may also be published by the drug regulatory department of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. The above information shall not be published without authorization.
The publication of drug safety information shall be timely, accurate, and comprehensive, and necessary explanations shall be provided to avoid misleading.
No unit or individual shall fabricate or disseminate false drug safety information.

People's governments at or above the county level shall formulate emergency plans for drug safety incidents. Drug marketing authorization holders, drug manufacturers, drug distributors, medical institutions, etc., shall formulate their own drug safety incident handling plans and organize training and emergency drills.
Upon the occurrence of a drug safety incident, the people's government at or above the county level shall immediately organize response work in accordance with the emergency plan; the relevant units shall immediately take effective measures to handle the situation and prevent the harm from spreading.

If the drug regulatory department fails to timely discover systemic risks in drug safety and fails to timely eliminate drug safety hazards within its supervision and administration area, the people's government at the same level or the drug regulatory department of the people's government at the next higher level shall conduct an interview with its principal responsible person.
If a local people's government fails to perform its drug safety duties and fails to timely eliminate major regional drug safety hazards, the people's government at the next higher level or the drug regulatory department of the people's government at the next higher level shall conduct an interview with its principal responsible person.
The interviewed department and local people's government shall immediately take measures to rectify drug supervision and administration work.
The interview situation and rectification situation shall be included in the evaluation and assessment records of the drug supervision and administration work of the relevant departments and local people's governments.

Local people's governments and their drug regulatory departments shall not restrict or exclude drugs produced by drug marketing authorization holders or drug manufacturers from other regions from entering their region by requiring drug testing, approval, or other means.

The drug regulatory department and its established or designated professional drug technical institutions shall not participate in drug production and business activities, nor recommend, supervise the manufacture, or supervise the sale of drugs in their own names.
The staff of the drug regulatory department and its established or designated professional drug technical institutions shall not participate in drug production and business activities.

If the State Council has other special management provisions for narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, toxic drugs for medical use, radioactive drugs, precursor chemicals for drugs, etc., such provisions shall apply.

If the drug regulatory department finds that a drug-related illegal act is suspected of constituting a crime, it shall timely transfer the case to the public security organ.
For cases where criminal liability is not required to be investigated according to law or exemption from criminal punishment is granted, but administrative liability should be investigated, the public security organ, the People's Procuratorate, and the People's Court shall timely transfer the case to the drug regulatory department.
If the public security organ, the People's Procuratorate, or the People's Court requests the drug regulatory department, the competent department of ecological environment, or other departments to provide assistance such as test conclusions, appraisal opinions, and harmless treatment of the drugs involved, the relevant department shall provide such assistance in a timely manner.
Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, if the act constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

If a person produces or sells drugs without obtaining a Drug Manufacturing License, Drug Distribution License, or Medical Institution Preparation License, the person shall be ordered to close down, the illegally produced or sold drugs and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than fifteen times but not more than thirty times the value of the illegally produced or sold drugs (including drugs already sold and unsold, the same below) shall be imposed; if the value is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan.

If a person produces or sells counterfeit drugs, the illegally produced or sold drugs and illegal gains shall be confiscated, the person shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification, the drug approval certificate shall be revoked, and a fine of not less than fifteen times but not more than thirty times the value of the illegally produced or sold drugs shall be imposed; if the value is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the Drug Manufacturing License, Drug Distribution License, or Medical Institution Preparation License shall be revoked, and no corresponding application shall be accepted within ten years; if the drug marketing authorization holder is an overseas enterprise, its drug imports shall be prohibited for ten years.

If a person produces or sells substandard drugs, the illegally produced or sold drugs and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than ten times but not more than twenty times the value of the illegally produced or sold drugs shall be imposed; if the value of illegally produced or wholesaled drugs is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan; if the value of illegally retailed drugs is less than 10,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the person shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification until the drug approval certificate, Drug Manufacturing License, Drug Distribution License, or Medical Institution Preparation License is revoked.
If the produced or sold prepared slices of Chinese crude drugs do not meet the drug standards but do not affect safety and efficacy, the person shall be ordered to make corrections within a time limit and given a warning; a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan may be imposed.

If a person produces or sells counterfeit drugs, or produces or sells substandard drugs with serious circumstances, for the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons, the income obtained from the unit during the period when the illegal act occurred shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 30% but not more than three times the income obtained shall be imposed; the person shall be prohibited from engaging in drug production and business activities for life, and the public security organ may impose detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days.
The raw materials, excipients, packaging materials, and production equipment specially used by the producer for producing counterfeit or substandard drugs shall be confiscated.

If a drug use unit uses counterfeit or substandard drugs, it shall be punished in accordance with the provisions on selling counterfeit drugs or retailing substandard drugs; if the circumstances are serious, the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other directly responsible persons who hold a practicing certificate for medical and health personnel shall also have their practicing certificates revoked.

Whoever knows or should know that the drugs are counterfeit drugs, substandard drugs, or drugs specified in Items 1 to 5 of Paragraph 1 of Article 124 of this Law, and provides convenience conditions such as storage and transportation for them, the entire storage and transportation income shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal income shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than five times but not more than fifteen times the illegal income shall be additionally imposed; if the illegal income is less than 50,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 50,000 yuan.
Article 121 The decision on punishment for counterfeit drugs and inferior drugs shall, according to law, specify the quality inspection conclusions of the drug inspection institution.

Article 122 Whoever forges, alters, leases, lends, or illegally buys or sells a permit or drug approval certificate document shall confiscate the illegal gains, and shall also impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if the circumstances are serious, shall also impose a fine of not less than five times but not more than fifteen times the illegal gains, and revoke the drug manufacturing permit, drug business permit, medical institution preparation permit or drug approval certificate document, and shall impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan on the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other responsible persons, and shall prohibit them from engaging in drug manufacturing and business activities for ten years, and may also impose detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days by the public security organ; if the illegal gains are less than 100,000 yuan, they shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan.

Article 123 Whoever provides false certificates, data, materials, samples or adopts other means to obtain by fraud such licenses as clinical trial license, drug manufacturing license, drug business license, medical institution preparation license or drug registration shall revoke the relevant license, shall not accept its corresponding application within ten years, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 5,000,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, shall impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan on the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other responsible persons, and shall prohibit them from engaging in drug manufacturing and business activities for ten years, and may also impose detention of not less than five days but not more than fifteen days by the public security organ.

Article 126 Unless otherwise provided for in this Law, if a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug business enterprise, drug non-clinical safety evaluation research institution, drug clinical trial institution, or the like fails to comply with the Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs, Good Supply Practice for Drugs, Good Laboratory Practice for Non-clinical Safety Studies, Good Clinical Practice, or the like, it shall be ordered to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and given a warning; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and it shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification, and even the drug approval certificate document, drug manufacturing permit, drug business permit, etc. shall be revoked; the drug non-clinical safety evaluation research institution, drug clinical trial institution, etc. shall not carry out drug non-clinical safety evaluation research or drug clinical trials within five years; and for the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other responsible persons, the income obtained from the unit during the period of the illegal act shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than ten percent but not more than fifty percent of that income shall be imposed, and they shall be prohibited from engaging in drug manufacturing, business, and other activities for ten years up to life.

Article 128 Unless a punishment is imposed according to law as for counterfeit drugs or inferior drugs, if a drug package is not printed or labeled with a label or accompanied by a package insert in accordance with regulations, or the label or package insert does not indicate relevant information or print the prescribed logo in accordance with regulations, it shall be ordered to make corrections and given a warning; if the circumstances are serious, the drug registration certificate shall be revoked.

Article 129 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, and a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug business enterprise, or medical institution fails to purchase drugs from a drug marketing authorization holder or an enterprise with drug manufacturing or business qualifications, shall be ordered to make corrections, and the illegally purchased drugs and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than two times but not more than ten times the value of the illegally purchased drugs shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than ten times but not more than thirty times the value of the drugs shall also be imposed, and the drug approval certificate document, drug manufacturing permit, drug business permit, or medical institution practice license shall be revoked; if the value of the drugs is less than 50,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 50,000 yuan.

Article 130 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, and a drug business enterprise fails to make records in accordance with regulations when purchasing or selling drugs, fails to correctly explain the usage, dosage, or other matters when retailing drugs, or fails to dispense prescriptions in accordance with regulations, shall be ordered to make corrections and given a warning; if the circumstances are serious, the drug business permit shall be revoked.

Article 131 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, and a third-party platform provider for drug online trading fails to perform the obligations of qualification review, reporting, stopping the provision of online trading platform services, or the like, shall be ordered to make corrections, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be ordered to suspend business for rectification, and a fine of not less than 2,000,000 yuan but not more than 5,000,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 132 Whoever imports a drug for which a drug registration certificate has been obtained, but fails to file with the drug regulatory department at the location of the port where drug import is permitted in accordance with regulations, shall be ordered to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and given a warning; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, the drug registration certificate shall be revoked.

Article 133 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, and a medical institution sells the preparations it has prepared on the market, shall be ordered to make corrections, the illegally sold preparations and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the value of the illegally sold preparations shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than five times but not more than fifteen times the value of the preparations shall also be imposed; if the value is less than 50,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 50,000 yuan.

Article 134 If a drug marketing authorization holder fails to carry out adverse drug reaction monitoring or report suspected adverse drug reactions in accordance with regulations, it shall be ordered to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and given a warning; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, it shall be ordered to suspend production or business for rectification, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed.
If a drug business enterprise fails to report suspected adverse drug reactions in accordance with regulations, it shall be ordered to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and given a warning; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, it shall be ordered to suspend business for rectification, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed.
If a medical institution fails to report suspected adverse drug reactions in accordance with regulations, it shall be ordered to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and given a warning; if it fails to make corrections within the time limit, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 135 If a drug marketing authorization holder, after being ordered to recall by the drug regulatory department of the provincial, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, refuses to recall, a fine of not less than five times but not more than ten times the value of the drugs that should be recalled shall be imposed; if the value is less than 100,000 yuan, it shall be calculated as 100,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the drug approval certificate document, drug manufacturing permit, and drug business permit shall be revoked, and a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed on the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor, and other responsible persons. If a drug manufacturer, drug business enterprise, or medical institution refuses to cooperate with the recall, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 136 Where a drug marketing authorization holder is an overseas enterprise, and the enterprise legal person designated by it within the territory of China fails to perform the relevant obligations in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the provisions of this Law on the legal liability of the drug marketing authorization holder shall apply.

Article 138 If a drug inspection institution issues a false inspection report, it shall be ordered to make corrections, given a warning, and a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed on the institution; the directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons shall be given a demotion, dismissal, or expulsion according to law, their illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, their inspection qualification shall be revoked. If the inspection results issued by a drug inspection institution are untrue and cause losses, it shall bear the corresponding compensation liability.

Article 139 The administrative penalties provided for in Articles 115 to 138 of this Law shall be decided by the drug regulatory departments of the people's governments at or above the county level according to their respective division of duties; the revocation of permits or the cancellation of license documents shall be decided by the original approving or issuing department.

Article 140 If a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug business enterprise, or medical institution employs personnel in violation of the provisions of this Law, the drug regulatory department or the competent health department shall order the dismissal and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 141 Where a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or medical institution gives or accepts kickbacks or other illegitimate benefits in the purchase and sale of drugs, or where a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or agent gives property or other illegitimate benefits to the person in charge, drug procurement personnel, physician, pharmacist, or other relevant personnel of a medical institution that uses its drugs, the market regulatory authority shall confiscate the illegal gains and impose a fine of not less than 300,000 yuan but not more than 3,000,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the market regulatory authority shall revoke the business license of the drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, or drug distributor, and the drug regulatory authority shall revoke the drug approval certificate, drug manufacturing license, and drug distribution license.
Where a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, or drug distributor bribes any state functionary in drug research and development, manufacturing, or distribution, the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible manager, and other liable persons shall be permanently prohibited from engaging in drug manufacturing and distribution activities.

Article 142 Where the person in charge, procurement personnel, or other relevant personnel of a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, or drug distributor accepts property or other illegitimate benefits given by another drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or agent in the purchase and sale of drugs, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a penalty shall be imposed according to law; if the circumstances are serious, the person shall be prohibited from engaging in drug manufacturing and distribution activities for five years.
Where the person in charge, drug procurement personnel, physician, pharmacist, or other relevant personnel of a medical institution accepts property or other illegitimate benefits given by a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or agent, the competent health authority or the institution shall impose disciplinary sanctions and confiscate the illegal gains; if the circumstances are serious, the person's practice certificate shall also be revoked.

Article 143 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law by fabricating or disseminating false drug safety information, which constitutes a violation of public security administration, shall be subject to public security administrative penalty imposed by the public security organ according to law.

Article 144 Where a drug marketing authorization holder, drug manufacturer, drug distributor, or medical institution violates the provisions of this Law and causes damage to a drug user, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.
Where a person suffers damage due to drug quality problems, the victim may claim compensation for losses from the drug marketing authorization holder or drug manufacturer, or may claim compensation for losses from the drug distributor or medical institution. Upon receiving a compensation claim from the victim, the person receiving the claim shall implement the first-liability system and make advance payment; after making advance payment, it may seek recourse according to law.
Where counterfeit drugs or inferior drugs are manufactured, or where such drugs are sold or used with knowledge, the victim or his or her close relatives may, in addition to claiming compensation for losses, claim punitive damages of ten times the purchase price or three times the losses; if the amount of additional compensation is less than 1,000 yuan, it shall be 1,000 yuan.

Article 145 Where a drug regulatory authority or a drug professional technical institution established or designated by it participates in drug manufacturing or distribution activities, the competent authority at the next higher level shall order it to make corrections and confiscate the illegal income; if the circumstances are serious, the directly responsible manager and other directly liable persons shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law.
Where an employee of a drug regulatory authority or a drug professional technical institution established or designated by it participates in drug manufacturing or distribution activities, the employee shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law.

Article 146 Where a drug regulatory authority or a drug testing institution established or designated by it illegally collects testing fees in the course of drug regulatory testing, the relevant government department shall order the return of such fees, and the directly responsible manager and other directly liable persons shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law; if the circumstances are serious, the testing qualification of the institution shall be revoked.

Article 150 Where a drug regulatory officer abuses his or her power, engages in malpractices for personal gain, or neglects his or her duties, he or she shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law.
Where there is dereliction of duty or malfeasance in investigating and punishing illegal acts involving counterfeit drugs or inferior drugs, the directly responsible manager and other directly liable persons of the drug regulatory authority shall be given severe disciplinary sanctions according to law.

Article 151 The value of goods provided for in this Chapter shall be calculated based on the marked price of the illegally manufactured or sold drugs; if there is no marked price, it shall be calculated based on the market price of similar drugs.
Article 152 The management of the planting, collection, and breeding of Chinese medicinal materials shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations.

Article 153 The administrative measures for regional folk customary medicinal materials shall be formulated by the drug regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the competent Chinese medicine authority of the State Council.

Article 154 The specific measures for the implementation of this Law by the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall be formulated by the State Council and the Central Military Commission in accordance with this Law.
Article 155 This Law shall come into force on December 1, 2019.
